- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Arctic is warming at a rate twice as fast as the global average, with a temperature increase of approximately 3°C (5.4°F) since the 1990s.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The extent of Arctic sea ice has declined by about 40% since the 1980s.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Arctic sea ice reached its second-lowest minimum on record in summer 2020, with some areas experiencing ice-free conditions for the first time.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Thawing permafrost is releasing methane, a potent greenhouse gas, into the atmosphere, with a warming of 1°C (1.8°F) over the past decade.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Arctic has seen an increase in wildfires, with 2020 being a record-breaking year.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Climate change is affecting Arctic ecosystems, including the migration patterns of animals like polar bears, caribou, and walruses.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended resources include the National Snow and Ice Data Center (NSIDC), NASA Climate Change, and the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC).
